source.title: Representational Simplicity and Circuit Size Dissociate in a Threshold-Dependent Way: A Controlled Test via Adversarial Training

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests representational simplicity and circuit recovery in GPT-2 Small, but it does not test the claim versions as stated: it does not assess neuron-pole job counts, explanations on held-out activating examples, automated neuron-explanation scores, or circuits built from neurons. Its circuit graph uses attention heads and MLPs.
record.gate_note: The study's own SAE reconstruction, feature-engagement, and circuit-recovery outcomes are recorded as results about representation and circuit complexity, but they do not directly measure any listed version. Cited findings from other work are excluded. The study reports no replacement-model comparison.
record.test_reason: The study compares SAE decomposability, SAE-feature attribution counts and EAP-IG circuit sizes (attention heads and MLPs) between standard and adversarially continually trained GPT-2 Small. It does not classify neuron poles by job, examine canonical polysemantic neurons, estimate interpretable-neuron shares, build neuron-level attribution graphs, or score neuron explanations. Its SAE and circuit measures are a related but different construct (representational and causal simplicity), so the results fit no version. 'Discusses' is kept because it engages the superposition/interpretability debate only in motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. One adjustment: the authors state that standard 'leads or ties below 85%'. The table shows standard leads at 70% and the models tie at 80% and 85%, while robust needs fewer edges at 90% and 95%. The authors also stress that the representational trend generalizes across a seven-model sweep and a FineWeb pair, but the high-faithfulness circuit result is shown only on the primary pair.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses adversarial continual training, SAE measurements, and EAP-IG circuit recovery, rather than neuron-pole job classification or explanation testing. It measures GPT-2 Small raw-graph subcircuits rather than neuron explanations.
record.method_sensitivity: Circuit comparison depends on the faithfulness threshold: the standard model reaches 70% with fewer edges, the models tie at 80% and 85%, and the robust model uses fewer edges at 90% and 95%. The 85% crossing is flat across the reported qualification sweep and FineWeb pair.

fits_no_version.finding: Adversarial continual training of GPT-2 Small gives lower SAE reconstruction error and fewer active SAE features in task attribution, but not more concentrated attribution once normalized by pool size. IOI circuit edge counts depend on the faithfulness target: standard leads at 70%, ties at 80–85%, and robust needs fewer edges at 90–95%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational/SAE simplicity induced by adversarial training does not uniformly translate into smaller faithful circuits; the comparison depends on the faithfulness threshold.

record.problems: One base architecture and one adversarial-training regime are studied. Circuit recovery is reported for a 200-prompt subsample, and the 90% and 95% circuit crossings are established only for the primary pair. The authors note that the GT comparison is not competence-matched. Circuit crossing counts are limited by the geometric search grid.
record.rows_left_out: Not every result in the seven-model qualification sweep was transcribed. Appendix D and Table 5 report sweep-specific SAE reconstruction, IOI candidate counts, α-ReQ, participation ratio, and 85% edge counts; these are outside the claim versions' named measures. GT circuit-curve values in Appendix G, Table 12, are not included because the authors explicitly do not use them as a competence-matched test. The paper's supplementary ablation-KL and EAP-GP results are also not included as neuron-pole or neuron-explanation tests.

untested.parts: No neuron-pole job categories or shares in any model.
Only GPT-2 Small; no neuron-share measure across models, scales or MoE.
No canonical polysemantic neuron (e.g., InceptionV1 cat/car) is examined.
The study varies training regime (adversarial), not architecture or tools. No interpretable-neuron share is measured; SAE compressibility is a different construct.
Circuits use heads/MLPs or SAE features, not individual neurons; there is no replacement-model comparison.
No neuron explanations or activation-prediction tests.

record.verdict_notes: Neither original source applies. No neuron-level analysis is performed anywhere in the text, so all rows are linked to 'none' and no verdict labels are given. Rows with 'observed' or 'partial' states were reset to cannot_determine because there is no version to check them against; the remaining rows are unchanged.

versions.untested_parts: No neuron-pole job categories or proportions are measured.
Only GPT-2 Small is studied; no neuron-pole shares across model scales, architectures, or MoE models are measured.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or shared-pose feature is tested.
No estimate of the fraction of interpretable neurons in InceptionV1-sized vision models is made.
Circuits are recovered from a raw graph of attention heads and MLPs, not from the model's own neurons; no comparison with a trained replacement model is reported.
The study does not test explanations against held-out activating examples or measure whether such explanations predict firing.
No automated neuron-explanation scores on new text are measured.
